_comment: Words ignored when deciding whether two titles share a term.
This is the one list on the site that is ours rather than Clarivate's, and it
is kept here in the open so it can be argued with. Everything else that
groups or filters a paper comes from Web of Science; this only decides which
lines get drawn between papers that are already placed.
Two kinds of word are listed. The first is ordinary English function words —
the, of, with. The second is research boilerplate that appears in titles
across every field and would link unrelated papers: understanding, comparing,
framework, empirical. Both say nothing about subject matter.
Words that look generic but are NOT listed, because in this lab they are the
subject: data, learning, information, network, science, knowledge, social,
graph, impact, classification, detection, prediction. A link on "data" plus
"science" is a real one here, and so is one on "suicide" plus "detection".
Matching is on lightly stemmed words, so network/networks and study/studies
collapse together and only one form needs listing.
